item.title: "I Can't Create A Battle Like This" - Miyamoto On The Origins Of NES Mario's Non-Violent Bowser 'Fights'

description.p: Lava to see it.We imagine that most of you here will have heard of a little game called Super Mario Bros., right? But how many of you have thought about how strange the big showdowns with Bowser are? As far as 'boss battles' are concerned, there's very little... battling. Well, in a recent press conference celebrating his Order of Culture award, Shigeru Miyamoto explained the thought process behind the game's jump-based finales."The most intriguing aspect of Super Mario, is that Mario doesn’t actually fight Bowser," Miyamoto told press at the conference (translated by Nintendo Everything), "Normally, if there’s a boss at the end, you have to fight him, right? But creating a battle is difficult, and we were really struggling with how to do it."Read the full article on nintendolife.com

item.title: Feature: 15 Years Ago, 'Return To Dream Land' Ushered In Kirby's Golden Era

description.p: Kirban legend.Kirby has always been one of Nintendo's more consistently successful franchises. While the little pink puffball never had anything remotely resembling a 'dark era' like many other Nintendo series, there was a time around the turn of the century where Kirby began to spin his wheelies a bit.After the 2000 release of Kirby 64: The Crystal Shards, developer HAL Laboratory immediately began work on Kirby’s next big adventure. Glimmers of a mainline Kirby title for the GameCube featuring the return of the helper system from Kirby Super Star with four-player co-op popped up in various circles over the years, including E3 2005, but a full-on game never materialised.Read the full article on nintendolife.com

item.title: Shigeru Miyamoto Becomes First Game Dev To Receive Japan's Prestigious Culture Award

description.p: Onward and upward!Adding to what is surely the most stacked roster of lifetime achievements, Shigeru Miyamoto is set to be awarded the prestigious Order of Culture award next month.The award, which first began way back in the 1930s, will be given by the Emperor of Japan on the nation's Culture Day (3rd November), and is awarded to those who have gone above and beyond in their contributions to Japan's art, literature, tech or science scenes.Read the full article on nintendolife.com
